CEST-detectable metabolite candidates: breast

1 of 6 candidates clear the simulated with-vs-without contrast threshold (0.5%) at some field strength, by chemical exchange (downfield, +ppm) or by the relayed NOE (upfield, −ppm). 2 fall below it; 3 are unknown because no group had a verified reference rate, so nothing could be simulated. The threshold applies to our own simulation, never to a literature MTRasym.

  • Mobile protein/peptide amide pool (APT): ✓ detectable (both)

  • myo-Inositol: ✗ not detectable
  • Taurine: ? unknown (not simulated)

  • Glycine: ? unknown (not simulated)

Excluded before simulation (not stored in the tissue): [model's own exclusion] Glycogen (glycoCEST): searched '<breast> glycogen concentration/glycoCEST'; breast is a lactational/secretory organ, not a glycogen storage depot, so no physiologically relevant tissue glycogen pool found in breast parenchyma -> noted absent.; [model's own exclusion] Glycosaminoglycans (gagCEST): breast stroma has proteoglycans (CSPG/DSPG, PMID 1711290) but no defined repeating-unit concentration in mM suitable for a gagCEST pool, and GAGs are a minor ECM component here -> not reported as a quantified candidate.; [model's own exclusion] Phosphocholine / glycerophosphocholine / total choline / PME / PDE: 31P/1H MRS category groupings lumping unrelated compounds, not a single simulable pool -> rejected.; [model's own exclusion] Creatine / total creatine: reported only as an MRS peak-grouping (tCr, Cho/Cr reference) with no defined single-molecule absolute value in the retrieved abstracts; treated as a spectroscopic category label and excluded per eligibility rules (the 31P phosphocreatine peak is 31P-only and off-target).; [model's own exclusion] Lipid CH2 / triglyceride fatty-acid peaks: 1H MRS peak groupings, not exchangeable-proton CEST molecules -> rejected.; [model's own exclusion] Bile/pancreatic/urine-type fluid metabolites: not applicable; breast has no such secreted-fluid CEST target in the parenchyma.; [model's own exclusion] Sphingomyelin family (PMID 33005404): reported only as a serum/tumor-correlation observation in a single resistant patient, no defined exchangeable-pool concentration -> rejected.; [model's own exclusion] Lactate / pyruvate / glucose: repeatedly detected in breast MRS (PMID 16229059, 30072394) but I could not retrieve a verbatim absolute tissue mM from the returned abstracts; excluded rather than invent a number.

Mobile protein/peptide amide pool (APT) — CEST: ✓ detectable (both)

Concentration: 250.00 mM typical (~200-300 mM (amide-proton-equivalent, per NH unit, estimated))

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: ESTIMATE. No source gives an absolute breast amide-pool number, so I derive the exchangeable-proton-equivalent concentration (the CEST-relevant quantity), NOT the protein's own molarity. Breast parenchyma has high protein content (~25 g/100 g, measured 25.65 g/100 g in poultry breast, PMID 37444172). 25 g protein ~100 mL = 250 g/L; at ~50 kDa/protein that is ~5 mM protein molecules, i.e. ~5 M of backbone residues, each contributing one amide (NH) proton. Only a minority of that is mobile/CEST-observable. A representative ~250 mM amide-proton-equivalent mobile pool (range ~200-300 mM) is adopted, consistent with the 2-3% APT MTRasym seen in human breast (PMID 23559550, 34477453). n_exchangeable_protons = 1 per NH-equivalent unit.

Derivation stepValueSource
Breast tissue protein content ~25 g per 100 g (measured 25.65 g/100 g in poultry breast).25 g/100 gjournal_article: PMID 37444172
Assume tissue density ~1 g/mL so 100 g ~ 100 mL; 25 g/100 mL = 250 g/L protein.250 g/Lcalculation
Convert to protein molarity at avg MW ~50 kDa -> ~5 mM protein molecules.~5 mM proteincalculation
Each backbone residue contributes one amide (NH) proton -> ~5 M of NH (residue) protons total (including insoluble fraction).~5 M NHcalculation
Only a minority of NH is mobile/CEST-observable; adopt representative ~250 mM amide-proton-equivalent pool.~250 mM (200-300)assumption

Recommended field strength(s): 0.5 T, 1.5 T, 3 T, 5 T, 7 T

Robustness to input uncertainty: robust

Uncertainty corners: Contrast over the uncertainty corners (mobile macromolecular aliphatic C-H (rNOE) [rnoe]: concentration 200-300 mM, kex fixed at 5 s−1 (single measurement, spread unknown); peptide backbone amide NH [amide]: concentration 200-300 mM, kex 15-158 s−1) at the swept B1/Tsat: 0.5 T: 1.89-2.80%, 1.5 T: 1.55-7.59%, 3 T: 2.12-10.21%, 5 T: 2.43-11.59%, 7 T: 2.21-15.07%. Threshold 0.5%. Detectable even at the low corner.

Frequency-collision analysis: At 1.5-7 T amide (3.5 ppm) well isolated: choline-OH (1.0) and myo-inositol-OH (0.72) >2 ppm away. Only warning vs semisolid MT pool (-2.4 ppm), broad (~16 kHz), handled by MTRasym baseline. At 0.5 T the rNOE (-3.5) blurs with choline-OH/myo-inositol-OH (95.8/89.9 Hz < 128 Hz), but at 1.5-7 T separation grows to 190-350 Hz. No self-collision: amide vs rNOE 7 ppm apart.

Direct water saturation: Direct-sat bandwidth: 10.6 Hz (0.5 T, 0.25 µT), 21.3 Hz (1.5-5 T, 0.5 µT), 31.9 Hz (7 T, 0.75 µT). Amide 3.5 ppm is 105-245 Hz from water at 0.5-7 T, well outside. rNOE -3.5 ppm similarly safe. No masking.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat: Amide kex 65.5 s−1 is a class-level median of two in-vivo brain/human measurements (PMID 40228056, 23008121); neither breast-specific. Breast tumor pH alters APT (PMID 31136039), so in-vivo breast kex could differ 2-3x. rNOE rate 5 s−1 from a protein-solution phantom (PMID 25996515), not breast tissue; in-vivo breast rNOE rate unknown. Confidence high only because amide dominates CEST across the full uncertainty corner (1.5-15%) and in-vivo breast APT is demonstrated.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 2.350% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Swept optimum at grid floor (0.5 µT): amide 65.5 s−1 is intermediate exchange, slow-exchange contrast maximized at low B1, eroded by direct water saturation above ~1 µT. Peak B1 shifts only weakly with B0. 3 s needed for quasi-equilibrium transfer.
    recommended sequence: 5.477% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Same physics as 1.5 T; B1 optimum unchanged at 0.5 µT. 3.5 ppm offset ~105 Hz from water, outside 21.3 Hz direct-saturation bandwidth. Slow/intermediate exchange keeps peak at grid floor.
    recommended sequence: 7.395% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — Identical to 3 T: kex/B0 ratio unchanged, B1 optimum holds at 0.5 µT. Contrast grows to 8.4% because the exchange-broadened peak sharpens with B0 and the offset-to-Hz separation doubles, moving the peak further from water's direct-saturation tail.
    recommended sequence: 8.386% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=3000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) — At 7 T the B1 optimum climbs to 0.75 µT because effective exchange (kex relative to B0) is slightly slower in the B0-scaled frame, shifting the low-B1 optimum up. Direct-saturation bandwidth widens to 31.9 Hz but 245 Hz offset at 3.5 ppm remains safe. 3 s still required for the 65.5 s−1 intermediate pool.
    recommended sequence: 8.957% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: With semisolid MT and rNOE at -3.5 ppm both present, MTRasym is inadequate: PMID 41553443 (murine breast, 9.4 T) showed MTRasym gave no subtype separation while MTRREX and AREX did. Recommend multi-pool Lorentzian difference (water+MT+amide+rNOE+background) or AREX with T1 map, per PMID 41553443 and PMID 37093984 (AREX-APT correlates better with fs than CESTR in tumors). At low B1 AREX also removes direct-sat bias.

Potential clinical impact

amide (APT, 3.2-3.6 ppm): 4 CEST/NOE application and 0 metabolite-change studies verified (2 human, 2 animal; 68 humans, 0 animals; 3 dropped by verification). APTw CEST is well supported in human breast cancer: it differentiates benign from malignant lesions at 3T (higher amide in malignant, AUC 0.932), aids TNBC subtyping and grading (higher APT in TN-type vs HER2+, AUC 0.874), and tracks neoadjuvant response. Murine models add malignancy, subtype, and immunotherapy-response evidence. The amide pool is itself the measured CEST quantity, so no separate metabolite-change MRS stream applies.

  • 250 mM mobile protein/peptide pool is consistent with breast tissue protein content. PMID 31136039 (n=22, 7 T) confirms APT in breast is dominated by mobile-protein concentration. PMID 31532006 documents the fat-artifact issue the simulation does not model. Concentration range 200-300 mM defensible.
  • Both groups classed correctly: backbone -CONH- is amide (3.5 ppm, intermediate); mobile aliphatic C-H is rNOE at -3.5 ppm. rNOE count 5 C-H/residue conservative. N-terminal amine mentioned in structure but not classed as its own pool; at 250 mM it is a small minority of amide protons, omission acceptable. No other neglected exchangeable protons. 3.5 ppm matches in-vivo APT shifts.
  • Simulated 3.5 ppm matches in-vivo APT shifts in human brain (PMID 23400954, 26845067, 25727379), human liver (PMID 26334509, 26391991, 32785767), rodent brain (PMID 24474497, 24496171, 28602944, 30553917, 37317709). Breast tumor APT imaging (PMID 31136039, 31532006) uses canonical 3.5 ppm. No discrepancy. N-terminal amine mentioned in structure but not simulated as its own pool.
  • At 250 mM ensemble it is a small minority of amide protons and is subsumed; omission acceptable. No other neglected groups. no SAR or hardware ceiling is applied: the recommended B1/Tsat is the sweep optimum, and deliverability must be checked against the scanner's SAR monitor Macromolecular CEST target (APT).

Concentration: 0.50 mM typical (~0.5 mM (ex vivo HR-MAS, estimated))

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: ESTIMATE. Free choline is a clearly detected and quantified 1H-MRS metabolite in breast tissue (ex vivo and 2D MRS; PMID 16229059, 19086016). It carries -OH (sn-glycerol) and -NH3+ protons, CEST-relevant. No verbatim absolute mM in retrieved abstracts, so I assign a representative ~0.5 mM and flag as estimated. Reported as the single molecule free choline, not the lumped 'total choline' grouping.

Frequency-collision analysis:

  • At every field, choline-OH (1.0 ppm) blurs with myo-inositol-OH (0.72 ppm): 5.9 Hz at 0.5 T, 17.6 Hz at 1.5 T, 35.1 Hz at 3 T, 58.5 Hz at 5 T, 82.0 Hz at 7 T - all far below the ~222.8 Hz combined linewidth. The two hydroxyl pools are inseparable at any field; only their sum is observable.
  • At 0.5 T choline-OH also blurs with APT-amide (53.2 Hz < 137.7 Hz) and APT-rNOE (95.8 Hz < 128.1 Hz). No self-collision (only one exchangeable group).

Direct water saturation:

  • Direct-saturation bandwidth: 4.3 Hz (0.5 T, 0.1 µT), 10.6 Hz (1.5 T, 0.25 µT), 31.9 Hz (3 T, 0.75 µT), 42.6 Hz (5-7 T, 1.0 µT). The 1.0 ppm offset is 30-70 Hz from water at 0.5-7 T. At 0.5 T the offset (30 Hz) is only ~7x the 4.3 Hz bandwidth - marginally safe.
  • At 3-7 T the offset (210-490 Hz) is well outside the 31.9-42.6 Hz bandwidth. The dominant issue is not direct saturation but the fast hydroxyl exchange self-broadening toward water.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat:

  • The hydroxyl kex 600 s−1 was borrowed from a myo-inositol measurement (PMID 20951217, human brain in vivo, 7 T, N=5), not from choline or breast. The abstract does not state whether k was measured in phantom or in vivo, and pH/temperature are not given. This is a class-level borrow; the in-vivo breast free-choline hydroxyl kex is unknown.
  • Alcohol hydroxyl exchange is strongly pH- and phosphate-dependent (PMID 32936483), so the 600 s−1 value could be off by 2-10x in breast tissue. The single measurement has no stated range, so no uncertainty corner was computed.

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: No field reached the 0.5% detectability threshold (max 0.014% at 7 T), so no sequence recommendation is warranted. If a future study attempted this, fast hydroxyl exchange at 1 ppm would need multi-pool Lorentzian fitting with dense Z-sampling (PMID 32936483) or AREX; MTRasym is inadequate at this offset due to MT and direct-saturation contamination.

Potential clinical impact

Choline (free choline): 0 CEST/NOE application and 3 metabolite-change studies verified (3 human, 0 animal; 150 humans, 0 animals; 0 dropped by verification). No free-choline-specific CEST/NOE imaging application in breast was found. Metabolite-change only: elevated total choline (tCho) in malignant breast tissue by in vivo and ex vivo 1H-MRS, and higher choline in TNBC vs TPBC. All MRS choline data are total-choline or composite 3.2 ppm resonances that do not separate free choline from phosphocholine/GPC.

Caveats / critique (8 points, 417 words) — 0.5 mM free choline in breast is reasonable; phosphocholine/glycerophosphocholine are the dominant choline-containing species in breast MRS, with free choline a…
  • 0.5 mM free choline in breast is reasonable; phosphocholine/glycerophosphocholine are the dominant choline-containing species in breast MRS, with free choline a minor fraction. The low concentration (0.5 mM, 1H) is the fundamental problem: even with favorable exchange, absolute contrast is tiny. Simulation confirms: <0.015% at all fields, far below the 0.5% threshold.
  • Agree on classing: single primary alcohol -OH correctly classed hydroxyl (fast exchange, ~1 ppm); quaternary trimethylammonium correctly non-exchangeable (no N-H). No other exchangeable protons. The chemist's 'negligible net CEST contrast' is confirmed by the simulation (0.001-0.014% across all fields). The 1.0 ppm shift is consistent with the hydroxyl band (PMID 38703021, 31366892, 28558795, 36432721, 34225021 all report 0.8-1.8 ppm).
  • No in-vivo breast free-choline-OH CEST measurement found; PMID 33103831's 1.5 ppm is from murine breast tumor GlcN-enhanced hydroxyl, not free choline - not directly comparable. The simulated 1.0 ppm shift matches the hydroxyl CEST band (0.8-1.8 ppm) from multiple phantom and in-vivo studies (PMID 38703021, 31366892, 28558795, 36432721, 34225021).
  • One outlier: PMID 33103831 reports 1.5 ppm in murine breast tumor after GlcN administration - but that is glucose/hydroxyl enhanced, not free choline. No free-choline-specific in-vivo breast CEST shift found. None. Free choline has only the single primary alcohol -OH (1H) as exchangeable; the quaternary trimethylammonium nitrogen bears no proton.

Frequency-collision analysis: At every field, myo-inositol-OH (0.72 ppm) blurs with choline-OH (1.0 ppm): 5.9 Hz at 0.5 T, 17.6 Hz at 1.5 T, 35.1 Hz at 3 T, 58.5 Hz at 5 T, 82.0 Hz at 7 T - all far below the ~222.8 Hz combined linewidth. The two hydroxyl pools are inseparable; only their sum is observable. At 0.5 T myo-inositol-OH also blurs with APT-amide (59.1 Hz < 137.7 Hz) and APT-rNOE (89.9 Hz < 128.1 Hz). No self-collision (single group).

Direct water saturation:

  • Direct-saturation bandwidth: 4.3 Hz (0.5 T, 0.1 µT), 10.6 Hz (1.5 T, 0.25 µT), 21.3 Hz (3 T, 0.5 µT), 31.9 Hz (5 T, 0.75 µT), 42.6 Hz (7 T, 1.0 µT). The 0.725 ppm offset is 22-51 Hz from water at 0.5-7 T. At 0.5 T the offset (22 Hz) is only ~5x the 4.3 Hz bandwidth - marginal.
  • At 3-7 T the offset (157-423 Hz) is well outside the bandwidth. Fast hydroxyl exchange self-broadening toward water is the dominant visibility limiter, not direct saturation.

Ex vivo / in vivo exchange-rate caveat:

  • The hydroxyl kex 600 s−1 and shift 0.725 ppm come from PMID 20951217, a myo-inositol-specific measurement but in human brain (not breast), in vivo, 7 T, N=5. The abstract does not state whether k was measured in phantom or in vivo, and pH/temperature are not given. This is a brain-in-vivo borrow; the in-vivo breast myo-inositol hydroxyl kex is unknown.
  • Alcohol hydroxyl exchange is pH- and phosphate-catalyzed (PMID 32936483), so breast pH (often lower in tumor, PMID 31136039) and ionic environment could shift kex by 2-10x. The single measurement has no stated range, so no uncertainty corner was computed.

Optimized saturation sequence by field strength (derived from a Bloch-McConnell B1×Tsat sweep):

  • 0.5 T: B1=0.1 µT, Tsat=750 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.005% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 1.5 T: B1=0.25 µT, Tsat=750 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.009% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 3 T: B1=0.5 µT, Tsat=1000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.022% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 5 T: B1=0.75 µT, Tsat=1000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.043% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied
  • 7 T: B1=1 µT, Tsat=1000 ms, continuous wave (CW-equivalent B1,rms from simulation sweep) —
    recommended sequence: 0.065% contrast; no SAR ceiling applied

B1/Tsat vs. extraction method (click for note + literature)

Note: No field reached the 0.5% detectability threshold (max 0.065% at 7 T), so no sequence recommendation is warranted. If attempted, fast hydroxyl exchange at 0.725 ppm would need multi-pool Lorentzian fitting with dense Z-sampling and a fat-suppressed or fat-corrected readout (PMID 31532006 for breast fat correction), or AREX. MTRasym is inadequate at this offset.

Caveats / critique (9 points, 426 words) — 0.5 mM myo-inositol in breast is on the low side; myo-inositol is a known breast MRS metabolite, typically higher in tumor than normal (PMID 27100284 lists it a…
  • 0.5 mM myo-inositol in breast is on the low side; myo-inositol is a known breast MRS metabolite, typically higher in tumor than normal (PMID 27100284 lists it among top-CEST-contrast metabolites in breast cancer cell-line extracts, with concentrations decreasing with aggressiveness). 0.5 mM may represent normal breast, not tumor; in tumor it could be 2-5x higher.
  • The simulated concentration is what was used, so if it is low the contrast is underestimated, but even at 2.5 mM the contrast would only reach ~0.3% - still below the 0.5% threshold. Agree: six secondary alcohol -OH groups correctly classed hydroxyl, fast exchange, ~1 ppm (simulated 0.725 ppm). No other exchangeable protons.
  • The 0.725 ppm shift comes from the myo-inositol-specific measurement in PMID 20951217 (human brain in vivo, 7 T, N=5). The chemist's 'weakly CEST-visible, small hard-to-isolate signal' is confirmed: 0.005-0.065% across all fields. At 0.5 mM and 6H the pool is small.
  • The simulation does not model the ring conformational averaging or the inequivalence of the six OH, but for CEST purposes the lumped 6H hydroxyl pool is a reasonable approximation. The simulated 0.725 ppm shift is the myo-inositol-specific value from PMID 20951217 (human brain in vivo, 7 T). No myo-inositol-specific in-vivo breast CEST shift was found.
  • The general hydroxyl band is 0.8-1.8 ppm (PMID 38703021, 31366892, etc.); 0.725 ppm is at the low end, consistent with the in-vivo brain measurement. None. Myo-inositol has six secondary alcohol -OH groups (6H) as its only exchangeable protons; all carbon ring protons are non-exchangeable C-H.

Taurine — CEST: ? unknown (not simulated)

Concentration: 1.00 mM typical (~1 mM (ex vivo HR-MAS, estimated from detection not absolute value))

Estimated concentration — no direct literature value found. Reasoning: ESTIMATE. Taurine is repeatedly quantified/detected in intact breast cancer biopsies by HR-MAS MRS (PMID 16229059, 23272149, 20101607) and is one of the prominent resolved peaks, alongside choline and creatine. However, the abstracts report relative ratios and trends, not an absolute taurine mM number. Taurine is a sulfur-rich osmolyte abundant in soft tissues (typically low single-digit mM). Given it is a clearly resolved ex vivo peak, I assign a representative ~1 mM (low-single-digit plausible) and flag this as an estimate pending an absolute quantification. It has -NH3+ (exchangeable ammonium) and -SO3H protons.

In vivo verification: ROI-differential CEST scan — axial (transverse), centred on the nipple-areola plane at the midpoint of the target breast

Why this scan:

  • The breast is a mixed gland/fat organ, so a single slice contains fibroglandular tissue (high protein/peptide) next to breast adipose and subcutaneous fat (low peptide, high lipid rNOE) and pectoralis muscle (high structured protein). The candidate pool is the mobile protein/peptide amide (APT) pool plus its relayed rNOE.
  • APT (3.5 ppm) and rNOE (-3.5 ppm) signal track protein content and cellularity, which differ sharply between these ROIs.
  • A generic MT/NOE background is roughly similar across soft tissues at a fixed offset, so if the +3.5 ppm asymmetry is high in gland/muscle and near zero in fat, while the -3.5 ppm peak is high in fat (lipid rNOE) and lower in gland, that concentration-tracking pattern confirms a real metabolite-specific exchange, not a uniform background dip.
  • This mirrors the with-vs-without logic as something measurable across same-FOV ROIs.

Scan protocol: 3 T, pulsed Gaussian train (duty-cycled rectangular train), B1=0.7 µT, 50 pulses × 50 ms (interpulse delay 10 ms, duty cycle 83.33%), total Tsat=3000 ms, TR=4000 ms

SAR reasoning (the experimentalist agent's own; the pipeline applies no SAR model):

  • SAR scales with B1^2 x duty cycle x Tsat. Mean saturation B1 = 0.7 µT; 83.3% duty cycle over a 3 s block (2.5 s RF on) gives a peak instantaneous power moderate, and a 4 s TR keeps magnetization partly recovered while spreading energy.
  • Over the small breast slice the local specific absorption rate stays within 2 W/kg whole-body / 4 W/kg IEC limits at 3 T, including the 1.3x B1 inhomogeneity re-simulation. The single-shot, low-flip readout after the block adds negligible extra RF.

Compromise rationale:

  • Only one candidate pool is actively targeted: the mobile protein/peptide amide (APT), for which the physicist recommended 0.5 µT / 3000 ms at 3 T.
  • I keep Tsat at 3000 ms and n_pulses/duty fixed so the block plus a single-shot readout fits in a 4 s TR, but raise B1 to 0.7 µT to (a) make the amide/rNOE contrast visible in the low-amide fat ROIs and (b) survive 0.7x-1.3x body-coil B1 inhomogeneity across the gland/fat/muscle ROIs.
  • This favors the amide pool and the rNOE lipid pool. Since APT is the only ranked candidate, nothing within the set is undersaturated; the trade is higher B1 (more SAR) for a more robust ROI-differential contrast.

Fat suppression: Water-selective (semi-selective water) excitation with a SPAIR fat-sat prepulse. This anatomy is dominated by fat (subcutaneous and intramammary fat), and lipid resonance tails ([-2,-4] ppm) directly overlap the -3.5 ppm rNOE pool and broaden the Z-spectrum, so fat must be suppressed to read both the amide and rNOE pools cleanly. SPAIR is robust to B1/B0 variation in the breast coil.

Motion mitigation: Prone breast coil, hand above head; cardiac-triggered (R-gated) or breath-hold free single-shot readout to suppress cardiac and respiratory motion; navigator for diaphragm/chest-wall displacement. Breast tissue is thin and the single-shot readout is short, but the inter-offset CEST sweep (13 offsets) adds scan time, so use cardiac gating rather than breath-hold to keep per-offset stability. Note Tsat is now ~3 s per offset.

Slice coverage: Axial slab, 3 slices x 6 mm (18 mm), centred on the nipple-areola complex of the target breast, oriented perpendicular to the chest wall (breast in prone, hand above head). Slab thickness covers the full anteroposterior breast so each slice contains, from skin to chest wall: subcutaneous fat, intramammary gland + fat, deep fat, pectoralis major, and a thin slice of anterior rib.

Structures in FOV: breast fibroglandular tissue, breast adipose tissue, subcutaneous fat, pectoralis major, anterior rib, axillary fat

  • -8.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference
  • -6.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference
  • -4.50 ppm: rNOE pool (mirror, Lorentzian baseline)
  • -3.50 ppm: rNOE lipid pool (-3.5 ppm), Lorentzian-difference reference (mirror of +3.5)
  • -2.50 ppm: fat tail / Lorentzian baseline
  • -1.00 ppm: Lorentzian baseline (mirror of +1)
  • +0.00 ppm: water (0 ppm), direct water saturation
  • +1.00 ppm: Lorentzian baseline

  • +4.50 ppm: Lorentzian baseline (mirror of -4.5)

  • +8.00 ppm: far-off baseline reference

Differential analysis plan:

  • For each ROI, average the Z-spectrum, correct B0/B1, and compute MTRasym(3.5) = [S(-3.5)-S(+3.5)]/(2*Sw) and the rNOE Lorentzian-difference at -3.5 ppm. Confirmation of the amide pool: MTRasym(3.5) follows the known protein gradient, highest in gland and muscle, low/near-zero in the two fat ROIs; and the +3.5 peak is absent in fat.
  • Confirmation of the rNOE lipid component: the -3.5 ppm Lorentzian-difference is highest in the fat ROIs and lower in gland. If MTRasym(3.5) were similar across all ROIs (flat), the effect is generic MT/NOE background, not metabolite-specific.
  • A significant gland-vs-fat contrast at +3.5 ppm with a fat-dominant -3.5 ppm peak, tracking the literature concentration differences, is the confirmatory pattern; a flat or inverted pattern is inconclusive.

Not actively targeted:

  • The ranked candidate list contained only one pool, the mobile protein/peptide amide (APT), so this scan is built entirely around it (and its coupled rNOE).
  • The other listed candidates -- myo-inositol, free choline, taurine, glutamate, glycine -- were not actively targeted: they had no/high simulated contrast at 3 T in the physicist agent's output, and their low mM concentrations with overlapping/weak peaks would be buried in the amide and fat-tail background on this single-compromise protocol, so they add no discriminating ROI-differential evidence here.

Caveats:

  • ROI partial volume is a real limit: gland and fat are interdigitated, so a 6 mm slice and small gland ROI will mix both, inflating the fat APT reading and blunting the differential. B1 inhomogeneity from the breast coil varies across gland/fat/muscle; even after B0/B1 (WASSR) correction the +3.5/-3.5 peaks shift, and the 0.7x/1.3x re-simulation bounds this.
  • Rib and air-bone susceptibility distort the Z-spectrum near the chest wall. One compromise B1/Tsat (0.7 µT, 3 s) cannot be simultaneously optimal for the amide and rNOE pools, and the low-amide fat ROIs depend on enough saturation to reveal near-zero signal.
  • Tsat is only 3 s (not 10 s) to fit the block+readout in a 4 s TR, so the absolute amide contrast is reduced versus a longer-saturation design, which the B1-scaled re-simulation also reflects.
  • Comparison-ROI concentrations are derived estimates, not direct assays; the design's validity rests on the concentration gradient being directionally correct, which the differential pattern test is built to verify.

  • uncertainty_corners: contrast re-simulated at the swept B1/Tsat at every corner of [concentration range from the literature agent] x [kex spread of the reference tier]
  • llm_sampling: each model's served defaults; the pipeline sends no temperature or top_p

A FAILED completeness check means the agent's structured output never covered everything it was asked to (e.g. a verdict for every metabolite) within its retry budget, and the incomplete output was kept; the deterministic checks above flag what is missing.
